newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Gasunie, Amoco finalise gas storage deal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Gasunie, Amoco finalise gas storage deal.

text.p: Dutch state gas monopoly Gasunie and Amoco Nederland on Wednesday finalised contracts enabling Gasunie to use Amoco's emergency gas stores in Alkmaar in the northwestern Netherlands.
"We've reached a final agreement on all contracts and we will start filling (the storage) with gas in November. We will be able to use it next (1997) winter," said Gasunie spokesman Abraham Warner.
Reduced supplies and lower pressure in Dutch gas fields has forced Gasunie to set up four swing storage facilities to meet peak winter demand.

Amoco Netherlands began construction of the storage tanks, at a cost of 300 million guilders, last November. The 500 million cubic metres of storage will provide an extra 24 million cubic metres of gas per day to supplement Dutch supply on occasional winter days.
"We could draw up to five percent of our daily needs from it for up to a couple of weeks each winter," Warner said.

Gasunie will have two other large storage sites, at Langelo and Grypskerk, which will supply more regularly in winter. Langelo will provide 80 million cubic metres from next winter and Grypskerk another 80 million the year after.
"We expect that, from next year, we will lack enough supply from our existing capacity," Warner said.
A fourth site, at Europoort near Rotterdam, will offer liquefied petroleum gas to meet hourly peaks of demand.
"Our hourly, daily and monthly needs will be covered by the four sites," Warner said.
